children: Sterling rises slightly after data showed U.K. retail sales unexpectedly returned to growth in August. Sales rose 0.5% in August compared to the previous month, beating the 0.1% decline expected by economists in a WSJ survey. It follows an unrevised 0.5% decrease in sales in July. The data come after the Bank of England voted 6-3 to leave interest rates at 3.75% Thursday but delivered tentative signals about raising rates in future. Sterling rises 0.1% to $1.3370 after the data, from $1.3361 beforehand. The euro trades steady at 0.8585 pounds, compared to 0.8590 before the data. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
